name: Trustworthy AI Assisted Scientific Simulation
goal: Identify published methods, frameworks, benchmarks and reproducibility practices that make an AI-assisted engineering simulation workflow more accurate, auditable and resistant to hallucinated or incorrect code, for a pipeline combining 3D Gaussian-splat reconstruction, Warp/MPM fluid-rigid simulation, CUDA/PyTorch GPU execution, mesh and SDF preprocessing, and Slurm execution on Lonestar6 A100 and Vista Grace-Hopper nodes. Identify concrete controls that reduce incorrect code, unsupported claims, provenance failures and false confidence in FORD / NO-FORD results.
summary:
EXECUTABLE SUCCESS IS NOT EVIDENCE OF PHYSICAL CORRECTNESS: LLM-generated simulation inputs can run and converge WHILE ENCODING THE WRONG EQUATIONS [Son26b], and agents frequently produce unstable or fabricated results in molecular dynamics [Kum26] and scientifically incorrect DSL workflows [Hol26].

HIGHEST-VALUE CONTROLS:
- Keep the agent at a CONSTRAINED ORCHESTRATION LAYER: validated structured specifications, retrieval from pinned repositories, deterministic adapters, validation-gated termination [Ho26]. Human-written solver templates with analytical and benchmark validation are a stronger boundary than unrestricted solver-code generation [Upa26].
- MAKE INTENT EXECUTABLE: encode governing terms, boundary and initial conditions, units, geometry and contact assumptions, and time integration in a MACHINE-CHECKABLE CONTRACT; compare generated configuration against it before expensive runs [Son26b]. Log every assumption explicitly, because simulator defaults remain invisible and undermine reproducibility [Lie26].
- Treat generated code as UNTRUSTED until independent checks pass. Evaluate correctness, numerical behaviour, algorithmic appropriateness, performance and library conventions, NOT MERELY COMPILATION OR TESTS [Zha26k]. DETERMINISTIC TYPED TOOLS CAN ELIMINATE RUN-TO-RUN ANALYTICAL VARIATION [Ada26b].

For Can It Ford the practical minimum is a pinned environment and repository manifest; immutable agent prompts, diffs, job scripts, seeds, GPU and software versions and outputs; mesh/SDF and conservation/units sanity checks; analytical or canonical regression cases; metamorphic tests for scaling, symmetry, resolution and timestep; checkpointed Slurm runs; and INDEPENDENT review of code, assumptions and FORD/NO-FORD evidence. RENDERINGS SHOULD REMAIN SEPARATE FROM SIMULATION ACCEPTANCE. AutoMat's 54.1 percent reproduction ceiling [Hua26] and AInsteinBench [Dus25] support building PROJECT-SPECIFIC benchmarks rather than trusting general coding-agent performance.
